name_note: Corynebacterium jeddahense is a rarely reported species; the retrieved literature describes its type strain and the genus, not its distribution on human skin.

sentences.text: Corynebacterium jeddahense is a Gram-positive, facultative anaerobic, nonsporulating bacillus, described as a new species within the genus Corynebacterium.
Its type strain was isolated from the faecal flora of a 24-year-old Saudi male suffering from morbid obesity, and has a 2,472,125 base pair genome.
Species of the genus Corynebacterium carry mycolic acids in their cell envelopes, which form the basis of a protective outer membrane called the mycomembrane.
In a genomic survey of 140 corynebacterial strains, more than half came from clinical material from humans or animals, which the authors took to show the pathogenic potential within the genus.
That survey also found that many corynebacteria lack the FAS-I system and must obtain fatty acids from their habitat, which it offers as an explanation of the lipophilic phenotype of some species.
